fit: oral sweet basil extracts and beam motor coordination in an ischemia model
assessment: The 2009 poster and 2011 journal abstract share researchers and endpoint but differ in reported occlusion duration. Overlap unresolved. The accessible outcomes give no stride estimate or fresh-food exposure.

fit: oral sweet basil leaf extract after cerebral ischemia in mice
assessment: Author abstract reports improved motor coordination and a neurological severity score after post-ischemia treatment. Detailed results, fresh herb intake and measured stride remain open.

fit: oral extract of dried tarragon leaves and forced-swim immobility
assessment: Both extract arms under restraint had lower immobility than restraint alone, with similar total maze arm entries. This comparison concerns a concentrated extract and stress behavior rather than a clinical depressive symptom.

fit: historical report of attempted use without verified hallucination outcome
assessment: An ethnobotanical article mentions alleged use with the intent to induce hallucinations. The description does not authenticate a marjoram species, clinical event, visual modality or preparation.

fit: tested oral marjoram extract and behavioral observation in rats
assessment: The Methods specify female rats and a dried aerial-parts extract. General observation and acute mortality do not measure hallucinations. No Parkinson or fresh-leaf exposure.

fit: ground anise mixture and open adverse-event ascertainment
assessment: The acute-COVID trial reports general symptoms including throat itching or thirst in the anise group. No prespecified fall endpoint or fall-frequency result.

fit: aniseed ether placebo excipient and a secondary falls outcome
assessment: Vitamin D doses were assigned against placebo in kidney disease. Falls are registered at six months, with no posted results or isolated ground anise exposure.

fit: thyme-containing topical oil blend and registered facial anxiety
assessment: The protocol registers a facial expression scale for anxiety in an intensive-care population, with no posted results, fresh thyme intake or Parkinson reduced expressiveness endpoint.
